lemma: K13-A(a). Let p be prime, q >= 2, T_q = {t in GF(p)^q : sum_i t_i = 0, t != 0}. Condition (L) for T_q: any two vectors of T_q have intersecting supports. Then (L) holds iff q = 3. Proof: (i) each t in T_q has |supp t| >= 2, since a single nonzero coordinate has nonzero sum. (ii) For q = 3, two vectors with disjoint supports would need >= 4 coordinates, but only 3 exist, so (L) holds. (iii) For q >= 4, t = e_1 - e_2 and s = e_3 - e_4 lie in T_q (sums are 0, entries are nonzero for every p >= 2) and have disjoint supports {1,2}, {3,4}, so (L) fails. Part (iii) is field-independent.
gap: Part (b): a replacement for (L) that still forces G[K_d] or a weaker subgraph for q >= 4 is OPEN. Part (c): an explicit basis beating the q=3 pattern is OPEN. Candidate direction for (b): a Hall-type condition on the support-intersection graph of the vertex block, not yet tested.

lemma: K13-A(a) repaired: for every prime p and every q >= 2, let T_q = {t in GF(p)^q : t != 0, sum_i t_i = 0}. Any two vectors of T_q have intersecting supports if and only if q in {2,3}. Proof: (i) every t in T_q has |supp t| >= 2, since a single nonzero coordinate has nonzero sum. (ii) q = 2: T_2 = {(a,-a) : a != 0}; every such vector has support {1,2}, so (L) holds for every p. (iii) q = 3: two disjoint supports of size >= 2 need 4 coordinates and only 3 exist, so (L) holds. (iv) q >= 4: e1-e2 and e3-e4 lie in T_q (sums are 0; the entries 1 and -1 are nonzero for every p >= 2) and have disjoint supports {1,2} and {3,4}, so (L) fails.
gap: Part (b) still open: a replacement for (L) for q >= 4 that still forces G[K_d] or a weaker subgraph. Candidate: a Hall-type / union-size condition |union of supports over X| >= (q-1)|X| (from dim T_q^X = q-1); not tested yet. Part (c) still open: an explicit basis beating the q = 3 pattern.
